summary: Okta affiliation attribute changed to array; ephemeral oncall permission assignment fails and runbook approvals hang
description:
Issue summary:
Users rotating into the oncall role (ephemeral permissions issued by the runbook-service) are no longer receiving the oncall RBAC claims. This started after an Okta attribute normalization rollout that changed the 'affiliation' profile attribute from a single string to an array of strings.

Impact:
- Immediate: Oncall engineers cannot be granted ephemeral 'oncall' permissions via the runbook approval flow; approvals hang at 'provisioning' step.
- Business: Pager routing still fires but engineers report 'Access denied' when opening internal incident consoles and runbook tooling.
- Scope: ~12 oncall users in prod us-east over last 3 hours. No reports from staging.

Observed behavior:
- Runbook-service logs show mapping failure: "rbac: mapped group not found for claim 'affiliation'"
- Identity-proxy shows Okta assertion contains affiliation as JSON array: [\"engineering\", \"contractor\"] instead of single string. Our mapping expects a scalar and uses exact match.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Authenticate via Okta with a user who has multiple affiliations.
2) Trigger a runbook approval that should issue ephemeral oncall role (runbook-service -> auth-proxy -> rbac).
3) Observe runbook UI stuck in 'Provisioning' and check logs for mapping errors.

Relevant logs (redacted):
- runbook-service ERROR 2026-03-12T17:02:04Z "rbac: mapped group not found for claim 'affiliation'" user=alice@redwood.ai runbook_id=RB-5532
- idp-proxy DEBUG 2026-03-12T17:02:03Z "okta assertion: {\"sub\":\"00u1abc...\", \"affiliation\":[\"engineering\",\"oncall\"] }"

Temporary workaround:
- Manual grant by infra-admins using the internal console worked for affected users (ticket-assigned ad-hoc).
- A stopgap mapping rule was applied in idp-proxy to take the first element of the array for affected runs, but it's not fully tested and was reverted at 2026-03-12T19:00Z.

Why this is likely:
- Okta attribute normalization change rolled out yesterday to handle multi-affiliations for contractors. Mapping validation in runbook-service assumes scalar claim and performs exact match against a group table. When claim is an array, mapping logic treats it as unmatched.

Requested outcome:
- Short term: re-enable safe fallback mapping for arrays (match any element) so ephemeral oncall issuance resumes.
- Long term: update RBAC claim mapping schema and add schema validation to detect claim type mismatches during attribute rollouts.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 17:10 - SRE (Marco Chen): Confirmed Okta assertion contains affiliation array for 8 affected users. Pulled recent IDP mapping change (Okta side) - change deployed 2026-03-11 22:45 UTC.

2026-03-12 17:35 - Auth eng (Priya Rao): Runbook-service mapping function rbac_mapper.go expects string and calls strings.TrimSpace; when value is JSON array, it serializes to '[... ]' and lookup fails. Unit tests didn't cover array case.
2026-03-12 18:00 - Security (Jonas Meyer): Confirmed no privilege escalation risk if matching any element in the array, but need audit logging for which element matched.

2026-03-12 18:20 - SRE (Marco Chen): Applied temporary feature-flagged change in idp-proxy to normalize affiliation -> string by choosing prioritized element 'oncall' if present. This restored provisioning for 6/8 users; two failed due to missing 'oncall' element.

resolution: 2026-03-13 10:00 - Fix merged: runbook-service now accepts affiliation claim as string or array and matches any array member against RBAC groups. Unit and integration tests added.
2026-03-13 10:30 - Deploy plan: canary to 5% of runbook instances in prod us-east, monitor provisioning success and audit logs for matched element. Rollout to 100% if no issues for 30 minutes.

Post-incident actions: update attribute mapping runbook in Confluence, add validation step to Okta attribute rollout checklist, implement alert when claim schema changes (type mismatch) detected by idp-proxy.
Follow-up: schedule a meeting with Identity team to coordinate attribute normalization changes and add an integration test in CI that validates claim types for critical RBAC claims.
